# Domainry Plane boundary

This Skill uses Domainry Plane only through the single packaged `domainry-cli` executable.

Choose one explicit `--environment <local|dev|stage|online>` or `--service <url>` target for `apply model` and Connector definition discovery. Keep that target fixed for the batch.

Release only with:

```text
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply model --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path <domain-qualified-module> [one target]
```

The command converges `backend/model/*.json`, checks the complete model, validates it with Domainry Plane, publishes the immutable delivery, and materializes or evolves the backend. Source preparation, implementation, tests, and `apply finalize` follow explicitly in the same apply stage. For an existing Builder delivery change, the first run may return exit 0 with `state: "evolution_review_required"` and `materialization_state: "not_materialized"`; this is a non-terminal control state and does not include a materialized implementation packet. Inspect its immutable audit path and SHA-256, then rerun its copyable `next_command` with a non-empty reviewed reason. Only `implementation_ready` or `applied` permits source work. A missing reason, mismatched or stale audit, or repair failure remains non-zero and fails closed. When successful reapply reports `evolution_source_finalization.state: "deferred_unfinalized_source"`, the audit proved that the old delivery had no finalization receipt; the in-progress source remains untrusted and must still pass the normal `apply finalize` gate. An existing finalization receipt's file SHA is audit-bound, so deleting or changing it after review makes the audit stale. Repair any other failed input or stage before rerunning the direct command.

Do not call Domainry Plane directly, reconstruct signing, hand-edit delivery state, or invent separate validate/publish/materialize commands. The current Builder flow keeps reviewed evolution inside `apply model`; it exposes no neighboring delivery-maintenance command surface.
# Project-owned source

Git owns project source. Edit, format, test, rename, and delete in-scope project source with normal development tools while preserving unrelated work. Treat a canonical Handler and its paired test as one review unit and keep both aligned with the same implementation-packet entry. `frontend/**` remains read-only except when an exportable Object SQL Report requires the Data Exchange export center and the TODO says `Frontend mutation scope: integration_authorized`; evidence that assigns any other defect to the frontend produces a finding with owner `frontend`, never an edit.

Allowed backend source includes `backend/go.mod`, `backend/go.sum`, `backend/actions/**`, `backend/config/**`, `backend/connectors/**`, `backend/domain/**`, `backend/i18n/**`, and `backend/tests/**`. The sole frontend allowance is the existing project's route/navigation, feature components, typed-client integration, localization, and focused tests needed for the export center in [offline Report export frontend](frontend-offline-report-export.md); do not mutate unrelated frontend source. Never edit `backend/generated/**`, `backend/cmd/**`, frozen contracts, Runtime manifests, receipts, caches, journals, packages, or other `.domainry/**` state. The only writable `.domainry` exception is the current session's `.domainry/development/<session-id>.md` TODO.

## Normal delivered-batch sequence

This is the only source sequence after `apply model` returns `implementation_ready` or `applied`. An exit-0 `evolution_review_required` response with `materialization_state:not_materialized` is not this boundary: inspect its immutable audit path/SHA, review the exact diff, rerun its `next_command` with the exact SHA and a non-empty reason, and gate again on the returned state. Missing review flags, a stale audit, and a failed evolution remain non-zero. Never read an old packet or continue implementation/finalization from the review-required state. A ready response may report `evolution_source_finalization.state:deferred_unfinalized_source` only for audit-proven never-finalized source; preserve and complete that source, but do not treat it as trusted—the ordinary focused tests and `apply finalize` remain mandatory.

1. Retain the exact `.implementation_packet.path`, delivery/materialization identity, file hash, returned `actions[]` direct-path index, `summary`, and `verification` reference from `apply model`. That command validates every delivered Action context, creates only missing canonical Handler/test skeletons, and persists immutable content-addressed context files under managed `.domainry/builder/**`.
2. Read the packet index once. Apply `summary.shared_constraints` to the whole batch, then for one Action at a time find its exact `action_key` and read that entry's `path` directly. The file is already the complete single-Action context, including only its referenced document content; do not run `jq`, reconstruct a document table, use `latest.json`, or read generated capabilities/context files directly.
3. Implement the complete Action-context Handler and paired test directly with normal source-editing tools. If either file changed concurrently, stop and reconcile both against the immutable context before continuing.
4. For an approved Connector source gap, load `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model capability --json --project <project> --connector-context <connector.provider>` immediately before implementing that Connector under `backend/connectors/**`. Action packet context does not replace Connector context.
5. Read the `verification.path` core, consume its complete `evidence_contract` and `setup_contract`, verify and read each listed `verification.minimum_read_plan` shard, copy `verification.harness_template.path` verbatim to `backend/tests/businessflow/harness_test.go`, and implement every required black-box case under `backend/tests/businessflow` before finalization. If test design proves the authored Action surface is insufficient, return to the Blueprint, run `model plan`, and follow `setup_contract.post_apply_repair` through audit review and reapply before resuming source work. Do not regenerate the shared transport/auth/fixture/evidence helpers. Implement other allowed project-owned backend source/tests and the authorized export-center exception. Never discard all call returns or any error/`ok` result in Handler or helper source; bind and handle it. Run the exact `summary.test_commands.focused` and `summary.test_commands.business_flow_compile`; they already carry the backend working directory, delivery build constraint, focused packages, project-local-plus-public hybrid proxy, and the finalizer's same-source read-only project check after focused Go tests.
6. Follow `summary.stage_boundary`: run `summary.test_commands.finalize` only after all project-owned source and both pre-finalize commands are complete, then run `summary.test_commands.full_tree`. Never use the full tree before finalization because the generated composition is intentionally incomplete at that stage. After successful finalization, freeze project-owned source for the verification attempt. Any source change starts a new repair iteration and requires focused tests, business-flow compile, and finalization again; never run `verify` against a stale receipt.

There is no second prepare, per-Action context, or source-write command.

The batch-prepared skeleton compiles against delivered capability types but intentionally returns `*.not_implemented`. It exposes missing implementation coverage and is never positive-path evidence. Replace the paired generated test's nil Execution call and placeholder oracle with typed non-nil Execution/capability stubs and assertions over current outputs and business effects; a generic no-panic assertion is not meaningful behavior evidence.

## Finalization boundary

After source/tests are implemented and every preceding implementation TODO item is closed, follow the packet's three command boundary without editing it. Finalization scans delivery-bound canonical Action source/test paths. A Handler paired with a generated test that still has nil Execution or an exact `*.not_implemented` oracle returns `state:"invalid"`; source-policy and applicable Go compile failures also fail closed. Finalize writes only its failure receipt on failure. Cross-module/full verification, packaging, and Runtime start require the current successful finalization. For business-flow work, the immutable `verification.path` core, its verified `minimum_read_plan` shards, and copied harness template replace repository or archive search and preserve the black-box boundary.

# Backend model files

`backend/model/*.json` is the only model-authored backend metadata input. The
model writes business differences; Plane expands every structural default into
the complete Ledger, Blueprint, authorization, Runtime Manifest, version and
hash contracts. Never edit `domain/**`, rendered Blueprints, or `.domainry/**`
by hand.

Omit every compiler-deterministic value: schema defaults, constants, one-value
enums, keyed identities, fixed discriminators, empty optional contracts and
derivable references. These are compiler output, not model decisions. Author a
field only when requirements permit more than one meaningful value or the
business meaning cannot be derived uniquely; validation must not turn a
compiler-owned default back into required model input.

## V3 file contract

The only top-level fields are `project` and `modules`. Exactly one file declares
`project`; modules and features may be split across files, but a Feature key and
a resource identity may each be declared only once across the whole model.
Unless an example is explicitly labeled a complete document or complete
Feature closure, a capability-reference JSON block is only a Feature-body
fragment: place it under `modules.<module>.features.<feature>`, add that
Feature's requirement, and resolve every referenced Object, Role, Action,
Workflow, Report, connection, or foundation target in the complete model.

Use this project-only fragment as `backend/model/00-project.json`:

```json
{
  "project": {
    "id": "item_submission",
    "name": "事项提交",
    "initial_workspace_administrator_role": "item_operator"
  }
}
```

A project-only fragment should omit `modules`; an empty `"modules": {}` is
accepted only on the same file as `project` for envelope compatibility. Do not
use that empty form in a feature-only file. A feature-only file omits `project`
and populates `modules.<module>.features.<feature>` with at least one Feature.

```json
{
  "project": {
    "id": "item_submission",
    "name": "事项提交",
    "initial_workspace_administrator_role": "item_operator"
  },
  "modules": {
    "core": {
      "features": {
        "item_lifecycle": {
          "requirement": {
            "statement": "操作员可以提交待处理事项。",
            "acceptance": [
              "提交成功后产生持久结果。",
              "失败时不得产生部分数据。"
            ]
          },
          "objects": {
            "item": {
              "fields": {
                "name": "text!",
                "status": "select![pending:待提交|submitted:已提交]=pending"
              }
            },
            "item_submission": {
              "fields": {
                "source_record_id": "relation!->item",
                "status": "select![recorded:已记录]"
              }
            }
          },
          "roles": {
            "item_operator": ["item.read;all", "item.submit;owner"]
          },
          "actions": {
            "item.submit": {
              "kind": "record_operation",
              "handler": {
                "reason": "必须原子更新事项并创建提交记录",
                "access": {
                  "item": ["get_for_update", "conditional_update"],
                  "item_submission": ["create"]
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The compact Role form is an ordinary human workspace role and expands
deterministically to `audience: "any"`, `assignment_mode: "manual"`, and
`provision_to_workspaces: true`. Use the extended Role object to declare other
metadata. A service-principal/system role must explicitly use its non-human
audience and `assignment_mode: "system_managed"`, and must omit
`provision_to_workspaces` (preferred) or set it to `false`. Bind an internal
Workflow/Scheduler execution role through Workflow `run_as`; do not change its
audience or assignment mode to make it a tenant-login role. It is never
rewritten into a human Role. Initial Workspace bootstrap materializes every
eligible human Role with `provision_to_workspaces: true`, while service and
system-managed Roles remain only in the complete post-bootstrap catalog. The
project must explicitly set `initial_workspace_administrator_role` to the Role
assigned to the first administrator. That selected Role must use `audience`
`any` or `user`, `assignment_mode: "manual"`, and no `required_binding_key`.
Do not infer it from `_admin`, risk level, permissions, declaration order, or
the first Role. Every model with a non-empty Workspace login-role directory
must select the Role; there is no historical fixed-role fallback.

```json
{
  "roles": {
    "workflow_worker": {
      "grants": ["item.read;all", "item.submit;all"],
      "audience": "service",
      "assignment_mode": "system_managed"
    }
  },
  "workflows": {
    "item_submission": {
      "enabled": true,
      "run_as": "workflow_worker",
      "trigger": {"type": "scheduled"},
      "action": {"type": "workflow_graph"},
      "trigger_contract": {"type": "scheduled", "object_key": "item"},
      "graph": {
        "nodes": {
          "start": {"type": "trigger"},
          "submit": {
            "type": "action",
            "contract": {
              "action": {"action_key": "item.submit", "on_error": "fail"}
            }
          }
        },
        "edges": {
          "start_submit": {"source": "start", "target": "submit"}
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The fragment assumes the referenced Object and Action exist in the complete
Feature closure. `provision_to_workspaces: true` means tenant login
materialization and is invalid on this internal role.

If this scheduled business flow evaluates an elapsed-time cutoff that must be
proved in a short-lived isolated Runtime, author the specific evaluation Action
with an optional standalone `evaluation_time: "datetime"` input from the first
Blueprint. The service-only Workflow Action may receive it in black-box
verification; the ordinary Scheduler path omits it, and the Handler uses real
current time when it is absent. Never turn this into a global clock override,
a human grant, or a startup historical fixture. The `scheduler.authoring`
`elapsed_time_verification` machine contract is authoritative for this seam.

## Delivery batches and file ownership

Whole-model validation does not require whole-product implementation. The files
currently present under `backend/model/*.json` are the complete desired-state
baseline for this delivery. A Delivery Batch is an authoring and verification
scope, not a loader or apply filter: preserve every previously applied model
file, then add or update only the batch's Feature files and declared
shared-resource closure. `model plan` and `apply model` continue to load and
validate the complete current model atomically.

Prefer `00-project.json` plus one Feature per descriptively named model file.
Several files may declare different Features under the same module. A Role,
entrypoint or other cross-cutting resource still has one owning Feature/file;
when it supports multiple Features, declare those stable keys through the
resource `requirements` override instead of repeating the resource.

The Feature key is also its Requirement identity. Moving one intact Feature to
another file does not change Ledger identity, but splitting or renaming a
Feature creates new Requirement identities, relinks affected resources and may
delete the old Requirement. Review that change with `model plan`; never treat it
as a mechanical file edit. For an already-applied oversized Feature, a valid
staged migration may retain the old Feature as a requirement-only umbrella,
move one resource group per batch to a new Feature, and temporarily link those
resources to both Requirement keys. Retire the umbrella only in a later,
explicitly reviewed destructive batch when it no longer represents accepted
product demand.

The V2 `items -> module -> kind -> item -> payload -> emits` envelope is not
accepted. Do not author `kind`, `status`, `depends_on`, `decisions`,
`requirement_keys`, `contract_version`, `capability_assembly`, or internal
Ledger item names. This project is not released yet, so there is no legacy
format fallback.

## Feature ownership and traceability

Every resource inside a Feature inherits that Feature's requirement. Plane
creates the requirement Ledger item, resource dependencies and behavior links.
Only a resource shared by multiple Features declares an override:

```json
{
  "objects": {
    "item": {
      "requirements": ["item_lifecycle", "audit_requirement"],
      "fields": {"name": "text!"}
    }
  }
}
```

`requirement` contains only `statement` and optional non-empty `acceptance`.
Behavior owner tuples and the no-executable reason are compiler output.

## Keyed identities everywhere

Every schema array whose item has a stable identity is authored as a keyed
object. The compiler sorts it, injects `key`, `id`, `object_key`, `path`, or
`connection_key` as required, and emits the strongly typed array. This includes
Objects, Fields, Roles, Actions, dictionary items, report parameters/result
columns, notification variables, Workflow inputs/nodes/edges and Agent
resources. An unchanged baseline Automation follows the same keyed-instruction
shape when it is loaded, but this Skill does not author a new Automation.
Repeating the identity inside a value or using an identity-bearing array fails
model loading.

Within a Workflow resource, `input_fields` and graph children remain keyed
maps (Actions use `input`, not `input_fields`):

```json
{"input_fields": {"comment": "long_text!"}}
```

```json
{
  "graph": {
    "nodes": {
      "start": {"type": "trigger"},
      "finish": {
        "type": "action",
        "contract": {
          "action": {"action_key": "item.finish", "on_error": "fail"}
        }
      }
    },
    "edges": {
      "start_finish": {"source": "start", "target": "finish"}
    }
  }
}
```

State transitions use their directed edge as identity, so duplicate edges are
structurally impossible:

```json
{"transitions": {"draft->submitted": "item.submit", "submitted->archived": {"workflow": "item.archive"}}}
```

Open maps remain maps. In particular Agent `input_schema`/`output_schema`
properties, Action/Workflow bindings, connector configuration and other
business dictionaries are not mistaken for resource arrays.

Author every platform-defined closed enum with its documented canonical
spelling (normally lower_snake_case; Report `currency` is lowercase). Plane
accepts mixed-case spellings for compatibility and canonicalizes them before
validation, including nested schema enums, Role scopes, Handler access
operations and field DSL vocabulary. This compatibility never applies to
identity-bearing keys or open business values; those retain their declared
case and stable identifiers remain strict lowercase.

## Field string DSL

Object Fields, Action `input`/`output`, Workflow inputs and Report SQL
parameters use the complete compact base grammar:

```text
<type>[!][->target][value[:label]|...][=default][;modifier[=value]]...
```

### Complete type and modifier quick reference

This is the single copyable reference for the field DSL. It contains every
supported field type and every Object-field modifier; capability references
should link here instead of repeating the table.

```json
{
  "active": "boolean=true",
  "amount": "currency!=0;precision=19;scale=2;currency=CNY;rounding=half_even",
  "effective_date": "date!",
  "starts_at": "datetime=2026-09-03T09:00:00+08:00",
  "contact_email": "email!;max_length=254",
  "quantity": "integer!;min=1;max=999",
  "remark": "long_text;min_length=1;max_length=500;localized",
  "score": "number;min=0;max=100",
  "discount_rate": "percent;precision=5;scale=2;rounding=half_even",
  "contact_phone": "phone;pattern=^\\+[1-9][0-9]{7,14}$",
  "customer_id": "relation!->customer;cardinality=many_to_one;on_delete=restrict;inverse=invoices",
  "status": "select![draft:草稿|done:完成]=draft",
  "business_no": "text!;unique;indexed",
  "website": "url",
  "assignee": "user",
  "category": "select!;dictionary=case_category",
  "risk_level": "select!;value_domain=risk_level"
}
```

- `!` means required.
- A default belongs in the base specification before the first modifier:
  `currency!=0;precision=19`, never `currency!;precision=19;=0`.
- `relation` requires `->target` and never accepts a default.
- `select` requires a non-empty, unique stable vocabulary. Labels default from
  the stable value when omitted.
- Supported non-relation Object modifiers are `unique`, `indexed`, `localized`,
  `min_length`, `max_length`, `min`, `max`, `pattern`, `precision`, `scale`,
  `currency`, `rounding`, `cardinality`, `on_delete`, `inverse`, `dictionary`,
  and `value_domain`.
- A relation never accepts `unique`; use `cardinality=one_to_one`, which makes
  the compiler derive uniqueness.
- Unknown types/modifiers, duplicates, invalid values, out-of-vocabulary
  defaults and context-inapplicable modifiers fail closed.
- Field types, modifier names and closed platform enum values are
  case-insensitive on input and compile to their documented lowercase values.
  ISO currency codes compile to uppercase. Stable business identities such as
  field keys, relation targets, option values, dictionaries and value domains
  remain strict lowercase identifiers.

Common repairs are local to the rejected field string:

| Rejected | Use | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"customer_id": "relation!"` | `"customer_id": "relation!->customer"` | A relation requires its target. |
| `"status": "select!"` | `"status": "select![draft\|done]"` | Select needs exactly one vocabulary source. |
| `"status": "select![draft];dictionary=status"` | Choose inline options or `dictionary`, not both. | Vocabulary sources are exclusive. |
| `"amount": "currency;precision=2;scale=3"` | `"amount": "currency;precision=19;scale=2"` | Scale cannot exceed precision. |
| `"amount": "currency!;precision=19;=0"` | `"amount": "currency!=0;precision=19"` | A default must precede every modifier. |
| `"starts_at": "datetime=2026-09-03 09:00"` | `"starts_at": "datetime=2026-09-03T09:00:00+08:00"` | Datetime defaults use RFC3339. |

The CLI rejects an invalid string during model loading and reports the stable
diagnostic code, exact JSON path, field key and repair facts. Fix that string;
do not replace the compact field map with generated full field arrays.

Notification variables use only the restricted `<type>[!]` subset. Their types
are `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`, `email`, `number`, `text`, and `url`; they do
not accept select options, relation targets, defaults, or modifiers. A business
enum such as `select![approved|rejected]` is rendered text in a notification, so
author it as `text!` and retain the enum on its owning Object or Action field.

Plane expands Object fields to `key`, `name`, `type`, `required`, `config`,
`validation`, labeled `options`, `unique` and `default_value`. Human-readable
names default from stable keys (`item_submission` -> `Item Submission`). Object
descriptions also receive a deterministic non-empty default; provide explicit
text only when it carries real domain meaning.

Action fields use the same strings. Object-only modifiers are consistency
assertions whose source Plane uniquely infers from the owning Object and the
Handler access closure, as detailed below. This preserves the named
type/precision contract without exposing source pointers to the model.

## Actions and source-owned Handlers

An Action key is exactly `<object_key>.<action_key>`; Plane derives
`object_key`, the default name, audit metadata, same-key Permission and empty
contracts. The model decides `kind`, allowed business roles, business fields,
preconditions and whether a source-owned Handler is needed.

`object_create` is the Runtime-owned generic single-Object create and must not
carry a project Handler. Use `object_operation` plus Handler/access when an
object-scoped create must derive trusted owner/org values, coordinate multiple
Objects, or execute other project logic. All other supported Handler kinds and
their object/record invocation scope are listed in the Actions capability
reference. A Handler Action must not use the bare suffix `create`, `read`,
`update`, `delete`, `restore`, `import`, or `export`, because those exact
`<object>.<operation>` keys belong to Runtime Object Permissions. Use a business
verb such as `lead.register` or a qualified key such as `lead.create_owned`;
grant that exact Action key to the Role.

```json
{
  "actions": {
    "invoice.approve": {
      "kind": "record_operation",
      "input": {"comment": "long_text!", "effective_date": "date!"},
      "output": {"status": "select![approved|rejected]"},
      "handler": {
        "reason": "Approval updates the invoice and durable decision atomically",
        "access": {
          "invoice": ["get_for_update", "conditional_update"],
          "approval_decision": ["create"]
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`handler.reason` is the only authored capability-gap/rationale statement.
Plane derives owner, trigger, scope, atomicity, rollback semantics, involved
Objects, read/write sets and transaction requirement. Do not author
`authorization`, `payload_fields`, `handler.data_access`, `handler.output`,
`audit_event`, empty defaults, or behavior tuples.

An aggregate-only Handler may omit `access` when it declares
`cross_workspace_aggregates`; Plane emits empty raw `data_access` and derives
the fixed source Object into the read-effect closure. Use the
`cross-workspace-aggregate` reading topic for the closed dimensions, optional
source-owned date bucket, measures, filters, authorization, result schema, and
Runtime limit contract. Grain, IANA time zone, and Workspace selection are not
caller input.

A Handler may likewise omit `access` when its complete effect is expressed by
the narrow Foundation capabilities `target_organization`,
`store_organization_catalog`, `store_organization_mutations`,
`workspace_identity_usage`, or
`identity_handler_delivery`. These declarations compile into fixed generated
methods and descriptor grants; they do not authorize raw Object reads/writes or
generic Identity/Organization APIs. Load the `organization-delivery`,
`identity-handler-delivery`, or `workspace-identity-usage` reading topic before
authoring one of them. Identity/Profile mutation effects needed by a declared
profile binding are compiler-owned closure and must not be repeated as
`handler.access`.

Keep a plain Action-only value as a plain field DSL such as `"reason": "long_text"`;
it does not need a backing Object field. When an Action field
uses Object-only modifiers (for example `max_length`) or Object-backed numeric
semantics, Plane infers its source from the owning Object plus the Objects in
`handler.access`, using the Action field's exact key only. The owning Object wins
over an equally named field elsewhere in the access closure; equally ranked
same-key fields fail as ambiguous. Plane never binds differently named fields
through Action verbs, prefixes, suffixes, stemming, edit distance, grammar, or
synonyms. When an Action input and persisted Object field represent the same
business datum, give them the same stable key, for example
`rejection_reason` end to end. Otherwise remove Object-only modifiers to keep
the Action value standalone. The diagnostic lists compatible rename candidates
without choosing one. Never author a source pointer or add a fake Object field.
This source is generated type/lineage reuse only; it does not copy an Object
field's runtime value into the Action payload.

For `identity_handler_delivery`, keep Identity-owned, non-Profile inputs such
as `login_id`, `display_name`, `role_key`, and `manager` standalone: use plain
DSL such as `email!`, `text!`, `select![employee|manager]`, or `user`, without
Object-only modifiers. A Profile-bound value may reuse Object-only modifiers
only when the owning Object or an Object in `handler.access` has an exact
same-key compatible field. Read the `identity-handler-delivery` topic for a
complete Action input and Profile example; never add a fake Object field.

Two fixed Store Organization mutation inputs are the deliberate exception to
same-key Object source inference. For an exact `rename` grant,
`store_name: text!;max_length=200` and
`expected_store_version: integer!;min=1` belong to the Identity capability and
remain standalone. For `disable`, only `expected_store_version` is required.
Do not add either field to the business Object just to satisfy source inference.
Business state uses its own record CAS input and `conditional_update`; the two
version tokens are distinct and both mutations remain in one Runtime Action
transaction.

Do not put protocol or infrastructure identifiers in Action input: `id`,
`request_id`, `trace_id`, `correlation_id`, `idempotency_key`, `workspace_id`,
`principal_id`, `record_id`, `route_id`, `tenant_id`, `session_id`,
`database_id`, `db_id`, and `row_id` are rejected. Record targets come from the
Action route, idempotency from `Idempotency-Key`, request identity from Runtime,
and new technical IDs from backend code. Stable business numbers remain
legitimate business fields.

## Roles, data scope and write ownership

Roles contain exact Permission grants, and every grant carries its own scope:

```json
{"roles": {"reviewer": ["case.read;org", "case.approve;owner", "case_attachment.read;owner"]}}
```

The only scope values are `all`, `owner`, `org`, `org_child`, and
`target_org`. The Role's same-key Action Permission is the only authored
allowlist. Plane reverse-derives `authorization.allowed_roles`, registers the
Action Permission definition, and never invents a Role grant or scope. Authoring
`Action.roles` is rejected as a duplicate source.

Object write policy is compiler-owned:

- an Object written by a Handler is `action_only` and has no Runtime CRUD
  behavior;
- every other Object is `direct_crud` and receives a Runtime CRUD behavior;
- a direct create/update/delete/restore Role permission or entrypoint mutation
  on a Handler-written Object is a blocking ownership conflict.

Plane expands Role grants into one scoped data-permission container per declared Role/Object.
That container is compiler-owned: the model declares each exact
Permission and scope once as `roles.<role>[] = "<permission_key>;<data_scope>"` and never repeats the
expanded Object policy.

Never author `config.write_policy`, role-level `data_scope`, `scope_overrides`,
`data_permissions` or `reference_permissions`. Handler roles use their explicit
same-key Action grant without receiving direct CRUD mutation permissions.

## Relation reference input

A `relation->target` field is also the complete model input for a reusable
reference selector. Plane derives an exact reference policy only when the role
can write the source Object and read the target Object; duplicate
source/field/target policies collapse to one stable identity.

The frontend calls
`GET /records/{sourceObjectKey}/fields/{relationFieldKey}/options`
with the raw user `query`. It never supplies a target Object, display field,
permission, SQL wildcard or `LIKE` expression. Runtime resolves the relation,
enforces the reference and target row/field policies, escapes `%`, `_` and the
escape character, then creates a parameterized case-insensitive contains
predicate. The component renders only the returned `{"id":"…","name":"…"}`
items.

## Report SQL

Prefer one source-owned file instead of an escaped SQL string:

```json
{"reports": {
  "part_usage": {
    "audience_roles": ["report_reader"],
    "object_sql_v1": {
      "sql_file": "backend/reports/part_usage.sql",
      "parameters": {"status": "text!"}
    }
  }
}}
```

The path must be exactly `backend/reports/<report-key>.sql`, canonical,
project-local and non-symlink. Plane normalizes line endings, hashes the source
and embeds SQL in the full Runtime contract. `sql_file` and `sql` are mutually
exclusive.

Plane derives the result schema and preserves SQL SELECT order. Optional
`result_schema` entries are semantic overrides keyed by SELECT alias and do not
control output ordering.

Quote every model-derived Object and field identifier with MySQL backticks,
including ``FROM `lead` l``, ``JOIN `order` o``, and qualified field references
such as ``l.`status```. This is mandatory even for ordinary stable keys: whether
the current parser treats a key as a keyword is not part of the authoring
contract. Keep aliases, parameter names, and result aliases as unquoted stable
keys.

Object SQL may reference only business fields explicitly declared under the
source Object's `fields`. Runtime-owned storage/scope columns
`owner_user_id`/`owner_org_id` are not project-declarable or Report-projectable
columns. Record-envelope `id` is available only as an internal JOIN, filter,
ordering, or COUNT operand and cannot be returned raw. Runtime applies owner/
organization permission scope before executing the Report. Every optional
`result_schema` entry overrides semantics for an existing SQL output alias.

Each `audience_roles` Role must grant `report.query.execute;all` as the exact
executable entry Permission, in addition to every source Object
`*.read;<requirement-selected-scope>` and required field-read policy. Audience
membership and source data access never authorize the Report query route by
themselves.

## Empty values and commands

Omit empty strings, arrays and objects. Omit absent `input`, `output`,
`permissions`, `config`, `preconditions` and optional collections; Plane
creates required empty internal structures. `false` and `0` remain legal only
when they are deliberate business values.

```text
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply model --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path <module> [--allow-destructive]
```

`model plan` is the no-HTTP repair loop. It runs the same loader, Ledger graph,
authoring checks, Project Contract projection, Runtime Manifest compiler and
source-owner validators used by apply. Its stdout `artifact` is a path relative
to the supplied `--project` root (also declared by
`artifact_relative_to: "--project"`), including on a non-zero repair result.
`apply model` atomically converges the
generated Ledger; an item absent from the model is a destructive deletion and
requires `--allow-destructive`.

Capability assembly remains progressive: choose from bounded summaries, load
only selected focused definitions, and let Plane compile ownership, module
closure and digests. Never author or cache a capability assembly in the model.

`templates/backend-model-handler-minimal/model.json.tmpl` is the directly
loadable two-Object Handler starter.

# Authorization and behavior ownership

Keep Action invocation, exact Permission grants, field policy, frontend
navigation, assurance and execution ownership separate.

In backend-model V3:

- the Role's exact `<action_key>;<data_scope>` array entry is the single
  authored Handler allowlist. Never write `Action.roles` or
  `authorization.allowed_roles`; Plane reverse-derives both the allowlist and
  the complete internal authorization contract from Role grants.
- `handler.access` is the minimum Object/operation EffectAuthority. Do not also
  write `handler.data_access`.
- an ordinary Role is an array of exact `<permission_key>;<data_scope>` strings;
  each Action or CRUD Permission has its own `data_scope`.
- Plane derives the Action Permission definition, reference policies, Handler
  EffectAuthority, behavior tuple and Object write policy. It never invents a
  Role grant or scope value.

Module HTTP entrypoints obey the same exact-grant rule. Before assigning a
verification step to an actor, look up the exact route in the implementation
packet's `verification.routes`; when `authorization.permission` is non-empty,
that actor's Role must carry `required_role_grant.compact`. An Object read/export
grant, Report `audience_roles` membership, Workflow assignment, or successful
login does not authorize a different executable entrypoint. In particular,
`GET /notification/inbox` requires `notification.inbox.list;all`, and
`POST /report/{reportKey}/query` requires `report.query.execute;all` in addition
to each source Object's requirement-selected `*.read;<scope>` grant. The Inbox
`all` grant selects the executable policy; Notification still binds durable
mailbox reads to the authenticated user and workspace.

```json
{
  "roles": {
    "case_reviewer": ["case.read;org", "case.approve;owner"]
  },
  "actions": {
    "case.approve": {
      "kind": "record_operation",
      "handler": {
        "reason": "Approval verifies eligibility and records a durable decision",
        "access": {
          "case": ["get_for_update", "conditional_update"],
          "case_decision": ["create"]
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Read operations are `get`, `get_for_update`, `optional`, `list`, `exists`, and
`count`. Write operations are `create`, `update`, `conditional_update`,
`delete`, and `restore`. Locking is not mutation authority. Existing-record
update/delete/restore requires `get_for_update` or `conditional_update`.

Use `object_operation` when no existing record target is supplied and
`record_operation` for a routed record target. Route record ID, workspace,
principal, request, trace and idempotency identities are Runtime/protocol
context and are rejected as Action business input.

A Handler-written Object is `action_only`; its allowed role must explicitly
hold the Handler Action's same-key scoped grant but no direct CRUD permission.
Every other Object is `direct_crud`. Never widen a role or add direct CRUD
merely to satisfy a Handler.

## Scope is an SQL mutation boundary

Treat data-scope enforcement as part of the repository operation, not as
response filtering. `all` means no additional data-scope `WHERE`; workspace,
caller filters and target IDs remain mandatory. Generated reads for `owner`,
`org`, `org_child` and `target_org` must combine the compiled predicate with
those conditions. Existing-record update, delete and restore capabilities must
first select the requested single ID or bounded ID batch with the same scope,
then execute the mutation with that predicate still present in its `UPDATE` or
`DELETE`. Batch target counts must match the authorized selection; any missing
or out-of-scope target fails the whole transaction without partial writes.

Never satisfy scope acceptance by loading unscoped rows and filtering them in
project code. Tests must prove an allowed ID succeeds, an out-of-scope ID is
unchanged, mixed allowed/denied batches roll back atomically, and the repository
query/mutation carries the compiled non-`all` predicate or proves that `all`
contains only workspace, caller-filter and target-ID conditions.

Organization claims are trusted Runtime facts,
not request fields or guessed headers. Sensitive fields remain fail-closed and
their explicit policy comes from the active Authoring Definition.

After implementation, map confirmed PRD authorization boundaries to focused
business-flow tests: actor, target, expected grant/scope, result or denial, and
unchanged durable state after rejection. Use real Identity-backed principals;
Blueprint declarations are not assignment evidence.
# Verification evidence levels

Read this contract during model/apply and before authoring `backend/tests/businessflow`; do not defer it until verify after project-owned source is frozen. The implementation packet's `evidence_contract` is the machine-readable marker grammar and flow-specific required-operation projection of these semantics.

Use this ladder for every verification check and final claim. Each level includes the lower levels, but an artifact reaches a level only when its current proof exists and is bound to the current source/model/Runtime identity.

## Ladder

- `L0_declared`: the capability exists in requirements, model metadata, or source. This proves intent only.
- `L1_delivery_verified`: source finalization is current; format, lint, vet, tests, and packaging pass through `verify`. This proves structural/release closure, not behavior.
- `L2_api_verified`: the operation executes through the real managed Runtime with a real session and its durable result is read back through the typed API or database. A denied/error/conflict case proves unchanged durable state; an idempotency case proves one effect after replay.
- `L3_scenario_verified`: every in-scope business-flow case executes end to end on real Runtime data. Each case starts from explicit preconditions, performs the ordered business actions, and observes its terminal durable result; requirement-defined denial, scope and failure branches are included.
- `L4_browser_verified`: reserved for the authorized offline export center when the project already provides a supported local browser verification path. Other browser-layer UI verification remains outside this Skill.
- `L5_restart_verified`: the critical L3 journey subset and sessions remain correct after a managed Runtime restart, with durable state read back and the critical cases rerun.

## Claim rules

- Never call L0/L1 output `verified`, `accepted`, `working`, `scenario_verified`, or `done`; say `declared` or `delivery_verified`.
- Never infer L2/L3 from a test name, source inspection, metadata checklist, `verify`, package receipt, Runtime health, HTTP 2xx alone, TODO prose, or TODO checker success.
- Never count a click, toast, queued job, emitted event, waiting Workflow, metadata-only import/export record, or local state change as the terminal business effect.
- Report skipped checks as skipped. Do not fold them into a higher level.
- Report coverage only with its exact include scope. A subset percentage is not whole-project coverage.
- Treat missing, empty, partial, stale, unbound, contradictory, or hand-written summary evidence as non-passing.

## L3 evidence requirements

For every business-flow case, bind project-local evidence to the current source digest and Runtime delivery identity. Record its requirement/flow ID, test name/path, actor/role, ordered actions, permission and data scope, persistence probe, terminal result, and audit/receipt identity when applicable.

For non-`none` data scope, provide at least two distinguishable owners and two scope groups when the rule separates them, plus records inside and outside the actor's allowed scope. A single actor, team, owner, or record cannot prove a scope boundary.

For mutations:

- success requires different before/after state and a successful read-back;
- denied, validation, and conflict cases require identical before/after state;
- idempotent replay requires the replay state to equal the first successful after-state;
- restart persistence requires the post-restart state to equal the accepted pre-restart state.

## Minimum terminal level

A Delivery Batch requires current L3 for every in-scope business flow and L5 for every changed or affected critical flow marked restart-sensitive. Unchanged flows may reference prior evidence only when it is still bound to the current baseline delivery/model identity; every changed flow and affected regression boundary must reach the same level in the current batch. Whole-product completion may be claimed only when no Requirement ID remains deferred. When the authorized offline export center changes frontend source, its focused tests and smallest relevant build/typecheck are mandatory; reach L4 only when the project already provides a supported local browser path. Other frontend-owned defects remain findings for the frontend owner.

## One verification model

Verification uses project-owned business-flow test cases and one CLI-owned,
temporary evidence protocol. There is no acceptance denominator, generic case runner,
carry-forward/stale-report workflow, or project-owned second evidence ledger.

Each current-batch business flow and affected regression boundary has one stable flow ID and one or more ordinary project-owned test cases under `backend/**`. Group cross-module cases under `backend/tests/businessflow/` when that makes ownership clearer; keep focused unit cases beside their source. A flow case starts from explicit preconditions, uses the requirement's real actor and scope, performs the ordered business actions, and asserts the terminal business result through durable read-back. It is not a list of disconnected endpoint checks. An unchanged flow may reuse prior evidence only when the TODO identifies that evidence and proves it remains bound to the current baseline delivery/model identity.

The current-batch business-flow inventory and affected regression closure must cover:

- every current-batch happy path from initial state through all required transitions to its terminal observable result;
- every requirement-defined alternate or rejection branch, including authorization, data-scope, validation and conflict behavior;
- unchanged durable state after a denied, invalid or failed action;
- idempotent replay, transaction rollback, concurrency, restart/resume, notification, schedule, file, integration, Object SQL Report, offline export submission, actor-owned job-list visibility or completed download only when the accepted flow actually depends on it;
- current-batch Requirement ID → Feature key → flow ID → test name/path traceability, plus baseline references for unchanged affected flows.

Do not multiply cases for platform internals that no business requirement observes. One flow case may prove several operations when they are steps of the same business journey. Conversely, do not call a set of isolated unit tests complete when no case executes the required journey end to end.

It closes only the Delivery Batch; whole-product completion additionally requires an empty deferred Requirement inventory. A genuinely unavailable external provider may be reported as `verification_blocked` only after every authorized local or sandbox route is exhausted; an ordinary failed case remains a repair finding. Successful CLI verification ends in `verified_and_stopped` with no managed Runtime intentionally left running.

Before completion, keep `Current stage: verify`. Change it to `done` only after the policy above is satisfied and the TODO evidence points to current CLI receipts and Runtime observations.

If the typed Data Exchange job-list operation is absent, keep the slice incomplete as an owner gap rather than substituting browser memory.

The final summary states the Delivery Batch identity and scope, delivery identity, changed files, current-batch and affected-regression test results, managed Runtime result, focused export-center frontend result when applicable, highest evidence level, deferred Requirement IDs, and explicit limitations. # Backend Runtime integration and managed proof

This reference covers the closed Runtime HTTP boundary, Action invocation, managed Runtime proof, and backend Handler coding idioms. Capability discovery comes from the CLI-compiled authority contract. Frontend dependency installation and package wiring remain outside this Skill except for the authorized Data Exchange export-center integration.

## Closed HTTP boundary

Project-owned backend source must not add, register, proxy, or require any application-facing HTTP interface. Do not create a project-local HTTP handler, router, controller, middleware endpoint, API facade, API proxy, serverless function, or alternate transport route. The authorized export center may wire only typed operations already published by the Application Delivery `runtime-domain-api-v1` contract; a missing Data Exchange job-list operation is a platform-owner gap, never permission to add or guess a route.

Custom source-owned Action Handlers expose no separate HTTP route; Runtime invokes them only through the published object or record Action operations below. Connector providers may perform contract-declared outbound calls through generated Connector APIs and governed transport, but they must not publish an inbound project API. If the published Runtime CRUD, Action, Report, file, authentication, or Connector contracts cannot express a required behavior, record the exact platform-owner finding and repair that owner in the same session instead of adding an HTTP endpoint; only the terminal policy's proved unrecoverable conditions permit stopping.

## Action invocation

Select object versus record invocation from the Runtime-published Action `kind`, using `runtimeActionInvocationScope`; never infer it from UI layout or from whether the execution owner is a custom Handler.

- `object_create`, `object_operation`, and `bulk_operation` use `runObjectAction` at `POST /records/{objectKey}/actions/{actionKey}`.
- `record_update`, `record_delete`, `record_restore`, `transition_state`, `conditional_update`, and `record_operation` use `runRecordAction` at `POST /records/{objectKey}/items/{recordID}/actions/{actionKey}`.

Business-flow tests wrap typed Action input as `{"data": <payload>}`; a bare payload is invalid for the Action invocation contract.

Call `listActions(objectKey)` first and pass the returned full `action_definition.key` unchanged to `runObjectAction` or `runRecordAction`; never shorten `group_class.book_group_class` to `book_group_class`. Use the exact storage values published by the Action input contract, such as `member`, not translated labels such as `会员`. A `record_operation` also requires the existing record ID in the record route; the presence of a button on an object list does not turn it into an object Action.

Frontends never call a generated Handler directly. Preserve the bounded Action input/output contract, workspace, bearer identity, request ID, idempotency key, assurance token, and concurrency value. Preserve Runtime result references and triggered workflows instead of reducing the response to a success boolean.

One accepted business intent must produce one Runtime mutation request. For example, “open table” is one declared Action call, not `create table session` followed by separate status, occupancy, audit, and notification mutations. Do not use `Promise.all`, sequential mutation hooks, retries with new keys, or a browser-side rollback to assemble one atomic backend command. Put the complete typed input on the Action and let its Runtime-owned unit of work perform all effects. Refetch/invalidation after the response and polling a returned job are allowed reads; they must not hide additional writes.

## Managed Runtime proof

Run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify --json --project <project> --address 127.0.0.1:<dedicated-port>`. It verifies and packages the project, starts the exact package to healthy state, stops it, restarts the same package/database cohort to healthy state, and finally stops it. A failure triggers best-effort cleanup of any Runtime started by that invocation. If it fails, remain in `verify`, repair the named owner, and rerun the same command. Never background-launch, discover arbitrary PIDs, kill unrelated processes, or add a separate Runtime-control step.

Runtime proof must cover declared allowed, denied, and scoped actors; Action effects; conditional conflicts; transaction rollback; idempotent replay without a second mutation or receipt; workflows/outbox; durable audit; and current delivery/package/Runtime receipt identity. `backend/tests/businessflow` is black-box: use only published Runtime HTTP/client operations, never direct project Handler calls, generated capability/data fakes, or database access. For each phase BF01-BF08 emit `DOMAINRY_BF_EVIDENCE=` rows exactly as specified in [verification](verification.md); CLI validation, not process exit alone, establishes the claimed flow observations. The managed child environment publishes the opaque Workspace, application, initial Workspace administrator login, Runtime-generated post-commit initial password, and independent changed password under `DOMAINRY_MANAGED_RUNTIME_*`. Copy the implementation packet's `verification.harness_template.path`; begin with its Workspace administrator helper, then create any flow-specific identities and organizations through authored Identity HandlerDelivery or OrganizationDelivery Actions. Use the mandatory initial password-change flow and never scrape logs, inject an actor graph, or reuse another cohort's identity. Use task-published database evidence paths only for owner diagnostics; project business-flow tests do not open them or rediscover private schema.

The implementation packet's route index is also the verification authorization
source. For each module route a test invokes, bind the real actor Role to that
route's exact `authorization.permission` and `required_role_grant.data_scope`
before finalization. Do not infer route access from a nearby Object Permission,
Report audience, or response schema. `GET /notification/inbox` needs
`notification.inbox.list;all`; `POST /report/{reportKey}/query` needs
`report.query.execute;all` plus the Report source/field permissions. Keep the
intentional denied actor without that entry grant.

Runtime's canonical record-list response is top-level `{"items":[...]}`. Each
record is an envelope such as
`{"id":"...","data":{"business_field":"..."},"updated_at":"..."}`:
read business fields only from `items[].data`, and retain `id`, `created_at`,
`updated_at`, and ownership metadata from the item top level. Do not probe
`items[].fields`, flatten top-level metadata into business data, or accept an
empty result caused by decoding the wrong shape.

A common login/read/catalog helper proves only that common precondition. Each case must then execute the Runtime operation sequence named by its requirement and read back its own terminal result. Human approval proof uses the declared Workflow process/task surfaces and both approved/rejected outcomes; calling approve/reject Handlers directly is not Workflow proof. Governed Report export proof uses Report query/prepare plus the requester-owned Data Exchange job and completed download, including unauthorized-role and cross-requester denial; a Report definition plus `*.export` permission is not export-control proof.

Successful `verify` returns `verified_and_stopped`; a running process, local HTTP response, or browser screenshot without matching delivery, package, database-cohort, and Runtime identity is not release evidence.

## Handler coding idioms (validated against the live Runtime)

These are Runtime-facing Handler constraints. `apply finalize` statically checks capability I/O in loops/recursion, bounded List pagination, handled capability results, and each `ConditionalUpdate` call's actual mutation argument. Unit and Runtime tests still own business semantics.

Generated Foundation capabilities are Action-specific, not service clients.
Target Organization resolution is fixed before mutation; store provisioning is
part of the same UoW; store and Workspace Identity catalogs accept only their
bounded page request; Identity delivery exposes only authored operations and
typed Profile bindings. Project source never supplies a Workspace set, trusted
profile relation, bearer, idempotency key, ownership column, or initial
password. Runtime may place a one-time initial credential into the declared
Action output only after commit and must mark that response no-store. Use the
generated Action context symbols, not Runtime internals or HTTP calls.

**True-batch invariant and finalizer preflight.** A multi-item command or query uses one generated batch/bulk capability call. Never call a single-item capability or Runtime API once per item in a loop, recursive cycle, callback, or loop-invoked helper and present the result as batch processing; that is pseudo-batch behavior and changes atomicity, latency, retry, and failure semantics. Prefer the generated `*Batch` operation for the complete bounded input. Pure in-memory loops are allowed only when needed to select items, construct bounded batch inputs, or correlate ordered results, and they must contain no capability I/O. If the required true-batch primitive is absent, record and repair the exact owning contract rather than disguising the gap. A bounded sequential fallback is allowed only when true batch cannot be implemented and the accepted requirement explicitly defines non-atomic ordering, partial completion, retry, and per-item failure behavior; record that reason and prove those semantics in tests.

`apply finalize` checks generated capability I/O in loops, callbacks, and recursive cycles, including capability aliases and named local helper call chains. Every List query uses `Page(page, pageSize)` with literal `pageSize` in `1..200`. Handle every result and error. Batch inputs are `1..200`, ordered one-to-one, and inherit the Action Workspace, Principal, grants, Scope, and transaction. Minimal shape:

```go
// Pure selection: capability I/O only outside loops.
orders, err := caps.RepairOrder.List(ctx, data.NewRepairOrderQuery().
    WhereStatusEqual(schema.RepairOrderStatusDispatched).
    OrderByIDAscending().
    Page(1, 200)) // literal page size, 1..200
if err != nil {
    return out, err
}
pending := make([]schema.RepairOrder, 0, runCapacity)
for _, order := range orders { // pure filtering loop: no capability calls here
    if len(pending) == runCapacity {
        break
    }
    if eligible(order) {
        pending = append(pending, order)
    }
}
queries := make([]data.DispatchReceiptQuery, len(pending))
for index, order := range pending { // pure request construction only
    queries[index] = data.NewDispatchReceiptQuery().
        WhereOrderIDEqual(order.ID).
        WhereBusinessDateEqual(businessDate)
}
exists, err := caps.DispatchReceipt.ExistsBatch(ctx, queries) // one call, outside loops
if err != nil {
    return out, err
}
// Build CreateBatch and notification DispatchBatch inputs in pure loops, then
// invoke each batch once outside loops and return every error unchanged.
```

**Build tag.** Backend compile requires the Domain SDK build constraint: a plain `go build ./...` fails on `verifiedDomainSDKBuildConstraint`. Run the implementation packet's exact `summary.test_commands`; they already carry the delivery-bound tag. The CLI's `verify` command also supplies it automatically. For a narrow manual diagnostic, read the exact `schema.DomainSDKBuildConstraint` value from `backend/generated/schema/revision.gen.go` and pass that unchanged with `-tags`; never guess it or scrape the generated tree.

**ConditionalUpdate requires a real condition.** Attach the compare-and-set condition observed under `GetForUpdate`; `apply finalize` checks the mutation argument at every call site:

```go
mutation := data.NewTicketUpdate(ticket.ID).SetAssigneeID(assignee)
if ticket.AssigneeID == nil {
    mutation = mutation.RequireAssigneeIDNull("ticket.assign.conflict")
} else {
    mutation = mutation.RequireAssigneeIDEqual(*ticket.AssigneeID, "ticket.assign.conflict")
}
updated, err := caps.Ticket.ConditionalUpdate(ctx, mutation)
```

`Require<Field>Equal/NotEqual/Null(errorCode)`, `WithExpectedUpdatedAt(...)`, and arithmetic `Increment*`/`Decrement*` effects satisfy the generated condition contract. Scaffolded or hand-written fakes must call `ValidateConditionalMutation`. On idempotent replay the predicate may legitimately differ; assert each execution's expected mutation rather than byte equality.

**NotificationIntent.SubjectVersion must be non-empty.** `runtimeext.NotificationIntent` fails `backend.notification.action_intent_invalid` when `SubjectVersion` is empty. Generated typed reads and mutation results expose `UpdatedAt`; mutation results receive it from the same canonical staged commit that Runtime persists. Use the subject record's `UpdatedAt` (including the value returned by `ConditionalUpdate`) as `SubjectVersion`; do not substitute transport metadata such as `request_id`, leave the field empty, or skip the dispatch.

**Transition Actions from Handlers or probes** must send the target state in the request payload (see `crud-and-state-machine.md`): a payload-less transition fails closed with 400 `backend.action.transition_payload_required`.
# Domain truth and settlement

## Requirement boundary

Freeze business facts before capability discovery. Platform capabilities decide how accepted facts map to Runtime; they do not decide what the facts are.

| Kind | Meaning | Implementation consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Occurred fact | A completed business event and its event-time inputs, rules, and result | Persist when it occurs; correct by reversal or adjustment |
| Summary | A read-only aggregation of occurred facts | Use Object SQL; never own the formula that created the fact |
| Simulation | A hypothetical result under assumed inputs or rules | Isolate from official facts, ledgers, payroll, and reports |

For every material calculation, decide: Calculation Owner, Evaluation Time, Persisted Result, Policy/Rule Snapshot, Input Snapshot, Calculation Trace, Correction/Reversal Strategy, Downstream Consumers, and Report Source of Truth. Keep only the smallest affected modeling slice blocked when accepted evidence leaves at least two incompatible choices that change the explicitly required formula, amount/unit semantics, occurred-fact identity, correction behavior, or observable result. Exact decimal representation, a stated threshold, and summation remain modelable when optional currency, unit, or range metadata is absent; use nullable metadata and stated command preconditions, and do not invent conversion rules. Route Runtime-owned representations through contract discovery and reversible persistence, index, audit, idempotency, and concurrency mechanics through the `safe_implementation_decision` rule in [requirements-and-domain-truth.md](requirements-and-domain-truth.md#critical-ambiguity); those choices do not become product business ambiguity, but their later verification remains mandatory.

## Versioned settlement pattern

```text
Versioned Policy
  → Atomic Settlement Action
  → Calculation Snapshot
  → Immutable Ledger
  → Reversal / Adjustment
  → Object SQL Report
  → Offline Data Exchange Export
  → Payroll / Export Reconciliation
```

Use this pattern for an event that locks money, commission, points, inventory cost, or payroll input. In one transaction, the settlement Action must validate idempotency and authorization, resolve the event-time policy, and persist policy identity/version, the actual rule snapshot, input snapshot, ordered calculation trace, final result, immutable ledger entries, and audit/outbox effects. A later policy version affects only later events.

Never update or delete an original financial ledger entry to correct history. Append a linked reversal for cancellation/refund and a reasoned adjustment for an approved correction. Preserve `reversal_of` or equivalent lineage, the original ledger ID, actor, time, reason, and approval boundary. A locked payroll/export consumer records the ledger IDs or a governed scope/hash it consumed; later adjustments follow the explicit correction period instead of silently changing the locked result.

## Anti-patterns

- Repeating one formula across pages or several reports.
- Joining current Settings to recompute a historical financial result.
- Rendering absent or unproven facts as numeric zero.
- Giving summary, detail, page, payroll, and export different scopes or formulas.
- Allowing Settings changes to drift historical results.
- Omitting ledger-ID-level traceability across consumers.
- Building a project-specific report AST, metric DSL, or SQL generator.
- Authoring Runtime Report transport or export-execution internals in the project model.
- Using a second export-only query, a synchronous browser export, or treating Runtime mechanics as domain facts.
- Synthesizing an export-job list from browser memory or internal Data Exchange tables.

## Acceptance matrix

Cover applicable boundaries with event-time input, policy identity, snapshot/ledger IDs, trace, consumer result, and allow/deny evidence:

- policy version switch before/after effective time;
- business-day cutoff and cross-midnight events;
- multi-party allocation with deterministic remainder handling;
- full/partial refund and reversal lineage;
- correction after payroll or another consumer is locked;
- summary/detail/page/payroll/export reconciliation by ledger ID;
- cross-store and cross-entity permission/data-scope denial;
- Runtime restart and Settings change without historical drift.
- Object SQL result correctness, parameter semantics, and source-of-truth reconciliation;
- actor-owned offline export submission, export-center visibility, completed download, and cross-actor denial when export is required;
- truthful active, completed, failed, cancelled, expired, and denied frontend states supplied by the published Data Exchange projection.

# Actions and transactions

Use a project-owned Handler only for named business behavior that plain Runtime
CRUD cannot express: conditional rules, derived writes, multi-Object atomicity,
governed state transitions, durable external intent, or typed project logic.

## V3 Action input

```json
{
  "actions": {
    "invoice.approve": {
      "kind": "record_operation",
      "input": {
        "comment": "long_text!",
        "effective_date": "date!"
      },
      "output": {
        "status": "select![approved|rejected]"
      },
      "preconditions": ["status == pending"],
      "handler": {
        "reason": "Approval validates eligibility and atomically records the decision",
        "access": {
          "invoice": ["get_for_update", "conditional_update"],
          "invoice_decision": ["create"]
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Action key has exactly one dot and its prefix is the owning Object. Plane
derives `object_key`, default name, audit value, same-key Permission,
`authorization.allowed_roles`, full payload/result field arrays, empty
contracts and generated Handler source identity.

Action kind also fixes invocation scope and execution ownership:

| Kind | Scope | Project Handler |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `object_create` | Object | Forbidden: Runtime-owned generic create |
| `object_operation`, `bulk_operation` | Object | Allowed for project-owned behavior |
| `record_update`, `record_delete`, `record_restore`, `transition_state`, `conditional_update`, `record_operation` | Routed record | Allowed for project-owned behavior |

When creation only maps declared fields into one ordinary Object, use
`object_create` without a Handler. When creation must derive trusted owner/org,
coordinate multiple Objects, or apply other project logic, use
`object_operation` with a Handler and its exact `access` declaration. Do not
name a Handler Action with the bare suffix `create`, `read`, `update`, `delete`,
`restore`, `import`, or `export`: those exact `<object>.<operation>` keys are
Runtime Object Permissions. Use a business verb such as `lead.register` or a
qualified key such as `lead.create_owned`, then use that exact key in Role and
workflow references.

The model must not author `object_key`, `payload_fields`, `authorization`,
`audit_event`, `handler.data_access`, `handler.output`, empty `defaults`, or
requirement behavior tuples.

`input` and `output` are keyed field-DSL maps. Omit them when empty. Relation
fields require `->target`; select fields require their stable value vocabulary.
A plain Action-only field needs no Object source. Currency and percent fields,
plus any Action field carrying Object-only DSL modifiers, ask Plane to infer a
source from the owning Object and the Objects declared in `handler.access`.
Plane uses only the Action field's exact key, preferring the owning Object over
an equally named field elsewhere in the Handler access closure. Differently
named fields are never bound through Action verbs, prefixes, suffixes, stemming,
edit distance, grammar, or synonyms. If an Action input and Object field carry
the same business datum, use the same stable key end to end—for example
`"rejection_reason": "long_text!;max_length=1000"` in the Action and
`rejection_reason` in every invocation. If the value is genuinely Action-only,
remove Object-only modifiers—for example use `"reason": "long_text"` instead
of `"reason": "long_text;max_length=1000"`. Missing or ambiguous exact-key
reuse fails with the actual DSL and a copyable replacement; compatible rename
candidates may be listed, but Plane never chooses one. Source reuse affects
generated type/lineage only and never copies an Object value into the payload.

This rule also applies to Foundation-capability input. For
`identity_handler_delivery`, Identity-owned non-Profile values such as
`login_id`, `display_name`, `role_key`, and `manager` use standalone DSL (for
example `email!`, `text!`, `select![employee|manager]`, and `user`) and must not
borrow Object-only modifiers. A business Profile value may reuse those
modifiers only from an exact same-key compatible field on the owning Object or
an Object in `handler.access`; see the complete copyable
[Identity HandlerDelivery](identity-handler-delivery.md) example.

`preconditions` is a closed Runtime expression grammar, not natural language.
The complete supported forms are:

- `field is present`
- `field in value1,value2`
- `field not in value1,value2`
- `field == value` and `field != value`
- `field > number_or_field`, `field >= number_or_field`, `field < number_or_field`, and `field <= number_or_field`
- `date_field >= today` and `date_field <= today`

For example, write `status not in converted,lost`, not “status is not converted
or lost”. Caller ownership belongs in the Role grant's `owner` data scope.
Related-record existence, cross-Object checks, and other complex conditions
belong in the source-owned Handler using the declared `handler.access`; do not
encode them as prose preconditions.

Never model `id`, `request_id`, `trace_id`, `correlation_id`,
`idempotency_key`, `workspace_id`, `principal_id`, `record_id`, `tenant_id`, or
`session_id` as Action input. Runtime supplies routed record target, actor and
workspace context; HTTP supplies request/trace/idempotency; backend code creates
technical IDs. A real order number or contract number belongs in the model
only when it is business data.

## Handler EffectAuthority

`handler.access` is keyed by Object and lists only operations the algorithm
actually uses:

- read: `get`, `get_for_update`, `optional`, `list`, `exists`, `count`;
- write: `create`, `update`, `conditional_update`, `delete`, `restore`.

Existing-record update/delete/restore requires `get_for_update` or
`conditional_update`. A friendly precheck does not replace an atomic
conditional mutation.

`handler.reason` must state the concrete business gap, not implementation
boilerplate. Plane derives involved Objects, exact read/write sets,
single-/multi-record scope, transaction requirement and rollback behavior from
access. Every written Object becomes `action_only`; all other Objects become
`direct_crud`. Direct CRUD grants or entrypoint mutation exposure on an
`action_only` Object fail model compilation.

Allowed roles are reverse-derived only from Roles that explicitly grant the
same-key Action Permission with a `data_scope`. The compiler projects the
Handler's minimum Object EffectAuthority from `handler.access`; the model does
not repeat Role scoped-Permission grants. The Handler does not bypass
authorization: generated capabilities apply `owner`/`org`/`org_child`/
`target_org` predicates and EffectAuthority inside the same host transaction;
`all` adds no data-scope predicate.

An Action may instead declare only `handler.cross_workspace_aggregates` and
omit `handler.access`. Plane derives each aggregate source Object into the
read-effect and authorization closure while keeping raw `Get`/`List` Object
APIs out of the Handler facade. The Object, fields, operations, filters, fixed
date-bucket grain/time zone, result schema, and hard limits are source-owned;
Runtime alone selects active installed Workspaces. Read
[cross-Workspace aggregates](cross-workspace-aggregates.md) before authoring
this capability.

Other capability-only Handlers may omit `handler.access` when they use only
Runtime-selected [target Organization/store delivery](organization-delivery.md),
[Identity HandlerDelivery](identity-handler-delivery.md), or
[Workspace Identity usage](workspace-identity-usage.md). Their source, operation
set, profile binding, output field, and page bounds are static model decisions.
Generated methods expose only those decisions; Runtime supplies actor,
installation scope, target ownership, transaction metadata, and other trusted
context. Do not repeat compiler-owned effect closure as raw Object access.

For every existing-record update/delete/restore, generated capabilities first
select the single ID or bounded ID batch with the exact Action scope compiled
into SQL, then retain the same non-`all` scope predicate in the atomic mutation.
Workspace and target-ID conditions remain mandatory for `all`. A mixed
allowed/out-of-scope batch fails without partial writes. Application-side
filtering is never authorization evidence.

## Connector calls and post-commit work

After the selected `email/smtp` connection is declared as `billing_email`, its
published durable operation is keyed by that connection:

```json
{"connector_calls": {"billing_email": "send_email"}}
```

Do not perform an irreversible synchronous external write inside the database
transaction. Persist a durable intent/outbox operation, commit local state,
then let the owning Integration/Notification worker deliver and reconcile it.
The Handler may return committed local evidence; it must not claim provider
success before provider evidence exists.

## Implementation sequence

1. Run `model plan`; fix the complete model diagnostic set.
2. Run `apply model`; read only the selected Action's generated context packet.
3. Implement the typed Handler with generated capabilities and one host-owned
   transaction boundary.
4. Preserve typed permission, scope, conflict and validation errors.
5. Test success, each accepted denial/conflict branch, rollback, replay and
   restart behavior required by the PRD.

Do not open a raw database handle, construct SQL, invoke Runtime over HTTP from
an embedded Handler, trust request identity fields, or manually reimplement
the generated authorization/data-scope checks.

For authoritative calculations, persist the policy identity/version, the
actual rule snapshot, the input snapshot and an ordered calculation trace with
the settled result. Never rewrite settled history after a rule change; produce
explicit reversal or adjustment entries linked to the original result.

# Permissions and data scope

Code-owned resources define the stable permission catalog. The backend model
defines application roles and business scope decisions. Identity owns users,
credentials, live assignments and principal resolution.

## Compact role input

Roles are keyed by stable identity. Each exact Permission grant carries its own
data visibility decision:

```json
{"roles": {
  "work_operator": [
    "work_item.read;owner",
    "work_item.export;org",
    "work_item_attachment.read;org_child;audit_denial"
  ]
}}
```

When a Role also needs metadata, use the extended object form and put the same
grant strings under `grants`:

```json
{"roles": {
  "work_operator": {
    "grants": [
      "work_item.read;owner",
      "work_item.export;org",
      "work_item_attachment.read;org_child;audit_denial"
    ],
    "field_permissions": {
      "work_item.private_note": {
        "read": true,
        "write": false,
        "export": false,
        "masked": true,
        "reason": "Private notes are not exportable"
      }
    }
  }
}}
```

`name` defaults from the role key. Every array item is an exact Permission key
and one of `all`, `owner`, `org`, `org_child`, or `target_org`, separated by a
semicolon. Append `;audit_denial` only when denied attempts must be audited.
Duplicate Permission keys are invalid. `grants` may be omitted from the extended
object when no explicit business grant exists.

The backend model must not declare role-level `data_scope`, `scope_overrides`,
`record_scope`, `data_permissions`,
`reference_permissions`, a root `permissions` collection, accounts, sessions,
users, assignments, or menu assignments.

## Compiler authorization closure

Plane preserves each authored scoped grant and validates the complete
authorization closure:

- `Action` -> the same-key Permission definition registered by Runtime;
- Role same-key Action grants -> the compiler-derived Action allowlist;
- explicit Object read/export/CRUD grants -> their own scoped grants;
- eligible relation fields -> exact source/field/target reference policies;
- Report and Export Control sources -> their validated functional/data closure.

The compiled Blueprint and Runtime Manifest contain only
`permissions[].permission_key/data_scope/audit_denial` for Role authorization.

A Handler-written Object is `action_only`. Its allowed roles explicitly grant
the same-key Action Permission, but do not receive direct CRUD mutation
permissions. Authoring such a direct permission is a blocking write-owner
conflict.

Field, export and guardrail policies remain explicit business exceptions and
use keyed maps wherever their schema has stable identity. Reference policies
are compiler-owned because relation target and role access are already known.
Custom data predicates are not part of role authoring. If none of the five
canonical scopes expresses the requirement, stop and surface a contract gap;
do not invent a sixth value or embed a predicate:

```json
{"roles": {"work_operator": ["work_item.read;owner"]}}
```

## Runtime ownership and verification

At apply, Plane publishes the generated project role catalog. Identity stores
current users and role assignments. Runtime evaluates the resolved principal,
exact scoped grant, field/reference policy and export policy on every
request.

Scope enforcement is storage-bound. For `all`, SQL keeps workspace, caller
filters and target IDs but adds no data-scope predicate. For the other four
values, list/read SQL combines the compiled scope predicate with caller filters;
update/delete/restore first select the requested single ID or bounded ID batch
within that scope, then retain the same predicate on the atomic mutation. Mixed
allowed/out-of-scope batches fail and roll back.
Application-side filtering of unscoped rows is never sufficient evidence.

Verification uses SDK-backed principals created through the supported Identity
test path:

- positive cases prove the exact Permission grant and matching `data_scope`;
- function-denied cases omit the permission or assignment;
- row-denied cases target a record outside the selected scope;
- rejected mutations prove durable state did not change;
- field/reference/export cases assert their exact masking or denial.

Never paste an SDK `AccessBundle`, `FunctionGrant`, or `DataPolicy` into
`backend/model/*.json`, and never provision a Blueprint user just to make a
test executable.
